proposed.explanation: Falsely assumes a complaint triggers automatic presumption of violation; the architect has the right to present evidence in defense. Reverses the evidentiary presumption; documentation supports innocence, not guilt. Understates the value of documentation; strong evidence can resolve a complaint favorably for the architect. Documentation of the architect's involvement during design development provides strong evidence supporting a claim of direct supervision. Emails directing design work, marked-up drawings showing review and feedback, and dated notes of design decisions demonstrate active participation. Such documentation significantly strengthens the architect's defense in professional discipline proceedings and helps establish that direct supervision was maintained. Documented evidence of active involvement in design meetings and drawing reviews provides strong proof of direct supervision compliance.
